newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PMP SAYS WELL PLACED FOR POSTAL COMPETITION.
newsitem.headline: PMP SAYS WELL PLACED FOR POSTAL COMPETITION.

text.p: Australia's PMP Communications Ltd on Wednesday unveiled plans to do battle with Australia Post if the state-owned behemoth ever lost its postal monopoly.
The direct-mail specialist, a major national distributor of advertising material to Australian homes, is lobbying for the collapse of the nation's "last great monopoly".
"I think it's a great opportunity for our company," PMP managing director Ken Catlow told an analysts' briefing.
The National Competition Council is considering submissions on the future of Australia Post's monopoly, and is to make a recommendation to government early next year.
Catlow said PMP would only enter the fray of deregulated postal services if the group could deliver bulk business mail, operate without price restrictions and use sub-contractors.
"If they are genuine about competing, they should not be frightened by a little company like us...," he said.
"The maximum we could glean would be 10 percent of the market," he added.
Australia Post has a monopoly over delivery of standard letters and mail under 250 grammes. Though there are some exceptions, the monopoly generates A$1.2 billion in revenue.
PMP, which already delivers to about 5.9 million homes or 96 percent of all Australian households, expects that revenue could be unlocked to competition by mid 1999 at the earliest.

"We are optimistic about it and I think the environment has never been better, and it's really the last great monopoly," Catlow said. "I think a bit of competition would be great for Australia Post and I think it would be great for us."
The National Competition Council is due to publish a position papaper on the issue of Australia Post's monopoly around October and November, PMP said.
